title: Japan 2-year JGB auction (No.489 inferred) — the last print that could have kept the 1-5y menu's 2-Year coupon channel alive, and cannot
source: EST: mof.go.jp English September 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2609e.htm), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 25,796 bytes) — its table row reads 'Sep. 30, 2026 | 2-year'. CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSAL THIS FILE REPLACES: that row carries NEITHER an announcement link NOR a result link — both cells are the plain string 'Detail' with no href, verified in the raw HTML this session. MOF publishes a 2-Year announcement at D-7 (No.488's was calendar/announcement/auct20260821e.htm for the 2026-08-28 auction, HTTP 200), so this auction's terms publish about 2026-09-23. The '(No.489)' is an INFERENCE, not MOF's print: the calendar prints an issue number only once announced (Sep. 1 '10-year (383)', Sep. 3 '30-year (91)', Sep. 8 '5-year (187)'; Sep. 15 20-year and Sep. 30 2-year carry none). The inference is mechanically reproduced from MOF's own 2026 calendars 2601e-2608e (8 x HTTP 200), whose 2-Year rows read No.481 Jan. 30, No.482 Feb. 27, No.483 Mar. 31, No.484 Apr. 30, No.485 May 29, No.486 Jun. 30, No.487 Jul. 30, No.488 Aug. 28 — one issue per calendar month with no gap, and Oct. 29 and Nov. 30 2-year rows following. Filed `estimate` on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office; the DATE is MOF's own and is not in doubt. Researched 2026-09-09 (docs/research/events/jgb-2y-auction-2026-09-30.md); discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of jgb-liquidity-enhancement-1-5y-2026-09-10
notes: Researched 2026-09-09 at D-21. THE PROPOSAL THAT CREATED THIS EVENT IS RIGHT ABOUT THE PAST AND BACKWARDS ABOUT THE FUTURE, AND THAT IS THIS ENTRY'S HEADLINE. It named the 2-Year roll 'the single largest mechanical driver' of the 1-5y liquidity-enhancement menu's >=1%-coupon composition drift. True retrospectively (the Jul->Sep roll moved the menu +1.71pp while every other sector held identical), but the channel is 93.0% spent: recomputing the whole 2026-09-10 menu from MOF's workbook this session reproduces the family's basis to the decimal — total 323.95tn, >=1% share 39.731%, sector shares 2Y 11.48 / 5Y 35.37 / 10Y 37.27 / 20Y 15.42 / 30Y 0.46% and >=1%-bucket shares 2Y 26.9 / 5Y 33.1 / 10Y 0.0 / 20Y 38.8 / 30Y 1.2% — and inside the 2-Year window (No.476-488) exactly ONE issue is sub-1%: No.476, 0.9%, 2,599.8bn. On the 2026-11-20 roll No.476 and No.477 leave and No.489 (this print) and No.490 enter; every remaining known issue No.478-488 is already >=1.0%, so the sector goes 100% >=1% and the channel closes. Sized: +0.85pp at the modal 2,800bn entrant (+0.78 to +0.95pp across the 8-print size range), against +1.71pp in September, then -0.04pp in January 2027 — halves, then zero. THE SATURATION MAP FOR THE WHOLE MENU, which is what the family actually needs: 20-Year and 30-Year are ALREADY 100% >=1%; 2-Year saturates 2026-11-20; the 10-Year window (No.348-363, 37.27% of the menu, the largest sector) is 0.0% >=1% — all sixteen issues carry a 0.1% coupon — and the first >=1% 10-Year ever issued is No.375 (1.1%, first issued 2024-07-03), which does not reach 1-5y remaining maturity until roughly mid-2029; the 5-Year is 37.2% >=1% and its last sub-1% issue is No.175 (0.9%, first issued 2025-01-15), leaving the window about 2029-01. So after 2026-11-20 the menu's >=1% share has exactly ONE live growth channel, the 5-Year bottom rolling off. This dates the sibling's unresolved leg: it could not separate composition drift from calendar time (collinear at +0.996, n=5), and the 2-Year channel dying in November is what breaks the collinearity. A SECOND FINDING, PROCEDURAL: the sibling computed No.488's eligible stock as 2,799.6bn from the main result page, whose Non-Price Competitive II cell prints '-'. The number is CORRECT — MOF's separate NPC-II page eresul20260828a.htm (HTTP 200), which no sibling cited, prints 0.0 — but the method carried an unrecorded exposure of up to 279.1bn, because that '-' appears even for auctions where NPC II was later nonzero (No.486's page shows '-' while the workbook carries 109.1bn; NPC II over No.481-487 ran 268.6 / 74.9 / 279.1 / 108.0 / 0.0 / 109.1 / 0.0bn, mean 120.0bn). For a 2-Year auction the 'a'-suffix page is the NPC II result; for a Liquidity Enhancement auction the same suffix is 'Issues Re-opened'. Read it before quoting a 2-Year issue's stock. THE COUPON RULE, TESTED: nominal coupon = the 2Y CME close rounded to the nearest 0.1%, which fits 7 of 8 on the prior session's close (the miss, No.482, was 0.4bp from the boundary) and 8 of 8 on the auction-day close. At 2Y = 1.848% on 2026-09-08 (MOF's own jgbcme.csv) No.489 sits knife-edge between 1.8% and 1.9%; boj-decision-2026-09-18 at D-12 is the dominant variable and the 2Y has already run +19bp since 2026-08-14. AND AUGUST WAS THE WEAKEST 2-YEAR PRINT OF 2026: cover 2.966 (2026 low, mean 3.885) with a 1.7bp tail (2026 high, median 0.55bp) and 93.31% allotted at the lowest price. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low`: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure, no house playbook is rates-keyed, and a front-end sovereign auction is the least market-moving instrument this calendar tracks. It sits one day after jgb-40y-auction-2026-09-29 and shares its date with government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 and pce-2026-09-30 (both high) — the auction clears in Tokyo hours, ahead of every US print listed. One dated adjacent event proposed in the same PR: jgb-2y-auction-2026-10-29 (No.490), the OTHER issue entering the 2026-11-20 menu, without which the saturation call is only half-tested. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
